excerpt: Somebody does something appalling. The usual response is that they should not have, and that something should now happen to them.

title: Reading Your Own Name in Numbers
excerpt: Almost everything in this material is asserted rather than shown.

title: Righteousness Is Right Plus Wise
excerpt: Righteousness is one of those words that has gone entirely moral. It means being good, or at least behaving as though you are, and it carries a faint smell of disapproval about other people.

title: Second Level Enchantments: Ensalmos
excerpt: The first enchantments act on a person to help them. Three of these four act on a person who has already been acted on by somebody else — and the assumption behind all three is that the victim may not know.

title: Second Level Invocations: Apelos
excerpt: This practice is solitary almost everywhere. One person in a quiet room, door shut, no non-magical people present.

title: Second Level Naturals: Telurikos
excerpt: The first-level weather charms are for somebody caught out — a flood, a lightning storm, a field that needs rain.

title: Second Level Protections: Guardos
excerpt: The first-level protections build boundaries — a circle, six walls, a companion, a binding.

title: Silver Against the Undead
excerpt: Everybody knows the folklore. A silver bullet for the werewolf, a silver blade for the vampire.

title: Stay Out of the Quarrel
excerpt: It happens in every community that has anything worth arguing about. Two figures you genuinely admire fall out, publicly, and within a week everybody has been sorted.

title: Telepathy Needs the Lower Self to Carry It
excerpt: There is a small family of things that get worse the more you apply yourself to them.

title: The Charge-and-Project Drill
excerpt: Read all ten school drills in a row and something becomes obvious that reading any one of them hides.

title: The Drop Counts Are Not Arbitrary
excerpt: Every oil recipe here specifies drops. Eight of mandrake, four of frankincense, two of dragon's blood.

title: The Esophoros Ring and the Lumen Score
excerpt: Almost nothing in this curriculum gives you a number. Durations are vague, the sphere finishes when it finishes, and most drills end in a change of perception nobody could check.

title: The Kudu and the Thorn Trees
excerpt: A tree has no brain, no nerves and nothing that could be called a decision.

title: The Magical Levels of an Incantation
excerpt: Every incantation in the spellbook sits under a heading that says First Level or Second Level.

title: The Magus
excerpt: Nine of the ten trades do something. They test formulas, catalogue creatures, call spirits, read cards, heal people, fight things, run rites.

title: The NN Slot
excerpt: In the middle of a Latin conjuration for water elementals, the sentence stops making sense.

title: The Psalm as a Power Source
excerpt: Open the spellbook at any entry and the same thing is sitting under the effect: a line of Latin, and a psalm number.

title: The Sword and the Unseen
excerpt: Nothing in this curriculum asks you to fight anybody. The schools heal, bless, find things out, calm situations and call helpful beings.

title: The Twelve Dimensions of a Conjuration
excerpt: Most of the working material here is small. Two or three Latin words, a psalm, an hour of the day.

title: The Voice of Ceremony
excerpt: A wedding, a funeral, a harvest festival. There are people standing in the room, and the words are said out loud so they can hear them.

title: The Voice of Magic
excerpt: The words are printed. Anybody can read them off the page. So what is left to get wrong?

title: The Wheel Is the Oath
excerpt: Everybody knows the wheel image. Life goes round, you are on it, and the usual advice is to stop clinging or stop wanting and it will let you go.

title: Thirty-Two Universal Laws, and How to Nullify One
excerpt: Everything in creation, formation and manifestation is governed by a law, or rather by groups of laws.

title: Toning and Tuning the Body
excerpt: Most people's relationship with their body is a series of complaints. It aches, it fails, it will not do what it is told, and attention goes to it only when something is wrong.

title: Yorde ha-Merkavah
excerpt: The instruction to look within is one of the emptiest things anybody says.

title: Atheism Is a Devout Belief in a Nothing-God
excerpt: Most arguments about religion are about whether the thing is there. One side says yes, the other says no, and both agree that the question is what matters.

title: Creation Is a Breath Still Happening
excerpt: Creation stories are told in the past tense, and the tense does most of the damage.

title: How to Read the Green and the Red
excerpt: An old text hands you a rule with no reasoning attached. Green means you failed.

title: Illumination, Initiation, Ascension, Transenation
excerpt: Hundreds of pages of formulas, metals, stones, oils, drills and rosters, and somewhere behind all of it there has to be an answer to the plainest question a beginner could ask.

title: Kefitzat ha-Derech and Invisibility
excerpt: Most defences of a mystical tradition quietly shrink it.

title: Lead and the Saturn Set
excerpt: Not a crisis exactly. The stage before that — when a situation is getting out of control, becoming too difficult, turning dangerous or altogether perilous and precarious, and you can feel it sliding.

title: Magic Is Maj Is Great
excerpt: Ask most people and you get a picture rather than an answer. Robes, candles, something appearing, something moving that should not move.

title: Magic Words Must Be in the Present Tense
excerpt: Because a request in the future tense doesn't stick. Words created in past or future tenses tend to get lost in the matrix of reality.

title: Number Four and the Tetractys
excerpt: Stand in a field with nothing in it. There is no north until somebody supplies one, no left, no far side.

title: Object, Sound and Image Concentration
excerpt: Try holding a single thought for sixty seconds without it changing shape.

title: Read the Zohar in Context First
excerpt: Open the Zohar anywhere and you'll find yourself in the middle of something.

title: Second Level Benedictions: Benedicci
excerpt: Most blessings, as people usually imagine them, are general. Good wishes, pointed at somebody, hoping for the best.

title: Second Level Divinations: Vates
excerpt: The first divinations handle the lost object and the person in front of you.

title: Second Level Healing: Curo
excerpt: ⚠ Nothing on this page is medical advice and nothing here replaces medical care.

title: Second Level Lights: Iluminos
excerpt: The first level of Lights turns a practitioner on and lets other people respond.

title: Sefer ha-Meshiv on the Descending Garment
excerpt: Traditions talk about revelation as though it simply arrived. Somebody was praying, or walking, or asleep, and something came — and the telling moves straight on to what was said.

title: Self-Exorcism Down the Toilet
excerpt: You are furious about something and the fury will not go. You have thought it through, you know it is out of proportion, and it is still there hours later, occupying you.

title: Six and the Union of Opposites
excerpt: A room you walk into and immediately want to leave. A situation that has not gone wrong yet and already feels wrong.

title: Spontaneous Song
excerpt: Almost everybody sings, and almost nobody makes a sound they have not decided on first.

title: The Eight Magical Directions
excerpt: Most of what happens to a person arrives unannounced. A bill, an offer, somebody turning up, something breaking.

title: The Four Cosmogonic Aspects in the Sphere
excerpt: The central instrument of this whole curriculum is not an object. It is a structure you build in your head and keep there — and the obvious objection is the one anybody would raise.

title: The Four Worlds Hold Four Things
excerpt: Tin goes with Thursday. Iron goes with Mars, and with the throat, and with a particular archangel.

title: The Hood Dissolves the Individual
excerpt: A surgeon scrubs and puts on the gown. A judge puts on the robe. A monk puts on the orange mantle.

title: The Master Numbers
excerpt: The numbers chapter gives a grid for each digit from one to ten — objects laid out in a configuration, charged with a formula.

title: The Practice of the Consciousnesses
excerpt: Almost everything in this curriculum has a procedure. Words to say, an hour to wait for, a metal to hold, a circle to draw, a stone to charge.

title: The Ring of Values
excerpt: The third and last of the inner rings is for pressure.

title: The Seven-Pointed Star
excerpt: Seven days in a week. Seven colours in a rainbow. Seven metals in alchemy, seven candles on the menorah, seven days of creation, seven archangels, seven planets you can see with your eyes.

title: The Smoking Censer
excerpt: A crystal ball will tell you about distant places, the past and the future.

title: The Ten Sefirot as a Code of Conduct
excerpt: A diagram can be studied for years without ever making a demand. You can know all ten spheres, all four worlds, every correspondence and every path.

title: The Uses and Types of Pentacles
excerpt: Three of the four weapons work the same way. Own one cup, one sword, one wand, charge whichever aspect you need today, and the same object serves for everything.

title: The Uses and Types of Swords
excerpt: There is a moment in any dealing with something powerful where the question stops being what do I want and becomes why should it listen to me.

title: The Water Vase
excerpt: Somebody has told you something and you do not believe it. You do not own a scrying ball, or you do and it is under linen halfway through its eleven days.

title: Two Minds at Once on Dunkirk Beach
excerpt: Not one after the other. Not calm underneath and frightened on the surface.

title: Suppression Makes Dynamite Into a Bomb
excerpt: There are two standard answers and they have been arguing for centuries.

title: The Rite of Noten Kavod
excerpt: The usual advice is about presentation. Stand differently, speak differently, set boundaries, expect better.
